- When sentiment is negative and price is trending down, model tends to underpredict — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model frequently overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture volatility — increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.5% to reflect uncertainty.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, model is underestimating — apply upward bias of 1–2% for next 5 days.
